name: AgenticSQL Golden Evaluation Benchmark
description: Benchmark dataset for multi-step agentic text-to-SQL evaluation across schema linking, AST validity, guardrails, execution accuracy, and grounded response synthesis.

test_cases.user_intent: List all customers who live in the USA ordered alphabetically by their last name.
test_cases.gold_sql: SELECT customer_id, first_name, last_name, email, city, country FROM customers WHERE country = 'USA' ORDER BY last_name ASC;

dialect_variations.sqlite: SELECT customer_id, first_name, last_name, email, city, country FROM customers WHERE country = 'USA' ORDER BY last_name ASC;
dialect_variations.postgres: SELECT customer_id, first_name, last_name, email, city, country FROM "customers" WHERE "country" = 'USA' ORDER BY "last_name" ASC;
dialect_variations.tsql: SELECT customer_id, first_name, last_name, email, city, country FROM [customers] WHERE [country] = 'USA' ORDER BY [last_name] ASC;

test_cases.description: Basic single-table filtering with exact WHERE condition and ORDER BY.

test_cases.user_intent: What is the total revenue and order count for each completed order status, grouped by customer ID, for customers with more than $300 in completed orders?
test_cases.gold_sql: SELECT customer_id, COUNT(order_id) AS order_count, SUM(total_amount) AS total_revenue FROM orders WHERE order_status = 'completed' GROUP BY customer_id HAVING SUM(total_amount) > 300.0 ORDER BY total_revenue DESC;

dialect_variations.sqlite: SELECT customer_id, COUNT(order_id) AS order_count, SUM(total_amount) AS total_revenue FROM orders WHERE order_status = 'completed' GROUP BY customer_id HAVING SUM(total_amount) > 300.0 ORDER BY total_revenue DESC;
dialect_variations.postgres: SELECT "customer_id", COUNT("order_id") AS order_count, SUM("total_amount") AS total_revenue FROM "orders" WHERE "order_status" = 'completed' GROUP BY "customer_id" HAVING SUM("total_amount") > 300.0 ORDER BY total_revenue DESC;
dialect_variations.tsql: SELECT [customer_id], COUNT([order_id]) AS order_count, SUM([total_amount]) AS total_revenue FROM [orders] WHERE [order_status] = 'completed' GROUP BY [customer_id] HAVING SUM([total_amount]) > 300.0 ORDER BY total_revenue DESC;

test_cases.description: Aggregation with WHERE clause on status and HAVING clause filtering aggregate sum.

test_cases.user_intent: Show each product name along with its category name and the total quantity sold across all completed orders.
test_cases.gold_sql: SELECT p.product_name, c.category_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_sold FROM products p JOIN categories c ON p.category_id = c.category_id JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.order_status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_id, p.product_name, c.category_name ORDER BY total_sold DESC, p.product_name ASC;

dialect_variations.sqlite: SELECT p.product_name, c.category_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_sold FROM products p JOIN categories c ON p.category_id = c.category_id JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.order_status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_id, p.product_name, c.category_name ORDER BY total_sold DESC, p.product_name ASC;
dialect_variations.postgres: SELECT p.product_name, c.category_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_sold FROM "products" p JOIN "categories" c ON p.category_id = c.category_id JOIN "order_items" oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN "orders" o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.order_status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_id, p.product_name, c.category_name ORDER BY total_sold DESC, p.product_name ASC;
dialect_variations.tsql: SELECT p.product_name, c.category_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_sold FROM [products] p JOIN [categories] c ON p.category_id = c.category_id JOIN [order_items] oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN [orders] o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.order_status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_id, p.product_name, c.category_name ORDER BY total_sold DESC, p.product_name ASC;

forbidden_hallucinations: Espresso Machine sold in completed orders
Air Fryer XL sold in completed orders

test_cases.description: 4-table relational join with status filtering and group-by aggregation.

test_cases.user_intent: Find all products that have never been reviewed by any customer.
test_cases.gold_sql: SELECT p.product_id, p.product_name, p.unit_price FROM products p LEFT JOIN reviews r ON p.product_id = r.product_id WHERE r.review_id IS NULL ORDER BY p.product_id ASC;

dialect_variations.sqlite: SELECT p.product_id, p.product_name, p.unit_price FROM products p LEFT JOIN reviews r ON p.product_id = r.product_id WHERE r.review_id IS NULL ORDER BY p.product_id ASC;
dialect_variations.postgres: SELECT p.product_id, p.product_name, p.unit_price FROM "products" p LEFT JOIN "reviews" r ON p.product_id = r.product_id WHERE r.review_id IS NULL ORDER BY p.product_id ASC;
dialect_variations.tsql: SELECT p.product_id, p.product_name, p.unit_price FROM [products] p LEFT JOIN [reviews] r ON p.product_id = r.product_id WHERE r.review_id IS NULL ORDER BY p.product_id ASC;

test_cases.description: LEFT OUTER JOIN with IS NULL predicate for anti-join / missing relationship pattern.

test_cases.user_intent: Which employees earn a base salary that is higher than the average base salary of their own department?
test_cases.gold_sql: WITH dept_avg AS (SELECT e.dept_id, AVG(s.base_salary) AS avg_sal FROM employees e JOIN salaries s ON e.emp_id = s.emp_id WHERE e.dept_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY e.dept_id) SELECT e.emp_id, e.first_name, e.last_name, d.dept_name, s.base_salary, ROUND(da.avg_sal, 2) AS dept_avg_salary FROM employees e JOIN departments d ON e.dept_id = d.dept_id JOIN salaries s ON e.emp_id = s.emp_id JOIN dept_avg da ON e.dept_id = da.dept_id WHERE s.base_salary > da.avg_sal ORDER BY s.base_salary DESC;

dialect_variations.sqlite: WITH dept_avg AS (SELECT e.dept_id, AVG(s.base_salary) AS avg_sal FROM employees e JOIN salaries s ON e.emp_id = s.emp_id WHERE e.dept_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY e.dept_id) SELECT e.emp_id, e.first_name, e.last_name, d.dept_name, s.base_salary, ROUND(da.avg_sal, 2) AS dept_avg_salary FROM employees e JOIN departments d ON e.dept_id = d.dept_id JOIN salaries s ON e.emp_id = s.emp_id JOIN dept_avg da ON e.dept_id = da.dept_id WHERE s.base_salary > da.avg_sal ORDER BY s.base_salary DESC;
dialect_variations.postgres: WITH dept_avg AS (SELECT e.dept_id, AVG(s.base_salary) AS avg_sal FROM "employees" e JOIN "salaries" s ON e.emp_id = s.emp_id WHERE e.dept_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY e.dept_id) SELECT e.emp_id, e.first_name, e.last_name, d.dept_name, s.base_salary, ROUND(da.avg_sal::numeric, 2) AS dept_avg_salary FROM "employees" e JOIN "departments" d ON e.dept_id = d.dept_id JOIN "salaries" s ON e.emp_id = s.emp_id JOIN dept_avg da ON e.dept_id = da.dept_id WHERE s.base_salary > da.avg_sal ORDER BY s.base_salary DESC;
dialect_variations.tsql: WITH dept_avg AS (SELECT e.dept_id, AVG(s.base_salary) AS avg_sal FROM [employees] e JOIN [salaries] s ON e.emp_id = s.emp_id WHERE e.dept_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY e.dept_id) SELECT e.emp_id, e.first_name, e.last_name, d.dept_name, s.base_salary, ROUND(da.avg_sal, 2) AS dept_avg_salary FROM [employees] e JOIN [departments] d ON e.dept_id = d.dept_id JOIN [salaries] s ON e.emp_id = s.emp_id JOIN dept_avg da ON e.dept_id = da.dept_id WHERE s.base_salary > da.avg_sal ORDER BY s.base_salary DESC;

forbidden_hallucinations: Dwight Schrute earns above department average base salary

test_cases.description: Common Table Expression (CTE) or correlated subquery calculating department average.

test_cases.user_intent: List all employees who do not belong to any department or do not have an assigned manager.
test_cases.gold_sql: SELECT emp_id, first_name, last_name, dept_id, manager_id FROM employees WHERE dept_id IS NULL OR manager_id IS NULL ORDER BY emp_id ASC;

dialect_variations.sqlite: SELECT emp_id, first_name, last_name, dept_id, manager_id FROM employees WHERE dept_id IS NULL OR manager_id IS NULL ORDER BY emp_id ASC;
dialect_variations.postgres: SELECT emp_id, first_name, last_name, dept_id, manager_id FROM "employees" WHERE dept_id IS NULL OR manager_id IS NULL ORDER BY emp_id ASC;
dialect_variations.tsql: SELECT emp_id, first_name, last_name, dept_id, manager_id FROM [employees] WHERE dept_id IS NULL OR manager_id IS NULL ORDER BY emp_id ASC;

test_cases.description: NULL checks using boolean OR on foreign key columns.

test_cases.user_intent: List all transactions with their source account name, destination account name, amount, and the actor ID who created them.
test_cases.gold_sql: SELECT t.txn_code, src.account_name AS source_account, dst.account_name AS destination_account, t.amount, t.txn_type, t.txn_status, a.actor_id FROM transactions t JOIN accounts src ON t.source_account_id = src.account_id JOIN accounts dst ON t.destination_account_id = dst.account_id LEFT JOIN audit_logs a ON t.txn_id = a.txn_id WHERE a.action = 'CREATE_TRANSACTION' OR a.action IS NULL ORDER BY t.txn_id ASC;

dialect_variations.sqlite: SELECT t.txn_code, src.account_name AS source_account, dst.account_name AS destination_account, t.amount, t.txn_type, t.txn_status, a.actor_id FROM transactions t JOIN accounts src ON t.source_account_id = src.account_id JOIN accounts dst ON t.destination_account_id = dst.account_id LEFT JOIN audit_logs a ON t.txn_id = a.txn_id WHERE a.action = 'CREATE_TRANSACTION' OR a.action IS NULL ORDER BY t.txn_id ASC;
dialect_variations.postgres: SELECT t.txn_code, src.account_name AS source_account, dst.account_name AS destination_account, t.amount, t.txn_type, t.txn_status, a.actor_id FROM "transactions" t JOIN "accounts" src ON t.source_account_id = src.account_id JOIN "accounts" dst ON t.destination_account_id = dst.account_id LEFT JOIN "audit_logs" a ON t.txn_id = a.txn_id WHERE a.action = 'CREATE_TRANSACTION' OR a.action IS NULL ORDER BY t.txn_id ASC;
dialect_variations.tsql: SELECT t.txn_code, src.account_name AS source_account, dst.account_name AS destination_account, t.amount, t.txn_type, t.txn_status, a.actor_id FROM [transactions] t JOIN [accounts] src ON t.source_account_id = src.account_id JOIN [accounts] dst ON t.destination_account_id = dst.account_id LEFT JOIN [audit_logs] a ON t.txn_id = a.txn_id WHERE a.action = 'CREATE_TRANSACTION' OR a.action IS NULL ORDER BY t.txn_id ASC;

test_cases.description: Double join on same table (source and destination accounts) with audit log linkage.

test_cases.user_intent: Show me the best performing products.
test_cases.gold_sql: SELECT p.product_id, p.product_name, COALESCE(SUM(oi.quantity), 0) AS total_units_sold, COALESCE(AVG(r.rating), 0.0) AS avg_rating FROM products p LEFT JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id LEFT JOIN reviews r ON p.product_id = r.product_id GROUP BY p.product_id, p.product_name ORDER BY total_units_sold DESC, avg_rating DESC;

dialect_variations.sqlite: SELECT p.product_id, p.product_name, COALESCE(SUM(oi.quantity), 0) AS total_units_sold, COALESCE(AVG(r.rating), 0.0) AS avg_rating FROM products p LEFT JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id LEFT JOIN reviews r ON p.product_id = r.product_id GROUP BY p.product_id, p.product_name ORDER BY total_units_sold DESC, avg_rating DESC;
dialect_variations.postgres: SELECT p.product_id, p.product_name, COALESCE(SUM(oi.quantity), 0) AS total_units_sold, COALESCE(AVG(r.rating), 0.0) AS avg_rating FROM "products" p LEFT JOIN "order_items" oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id LEFT JOIN "reviews" r ON p.product_id = r.product_id GROUP BY p.product_id, p.product_name ORDER BY total_units_sold DESC, avg_rating DESC;
dialect_variations.tsql: SELECT p.product_id, p.product_name, COALESCE(SUM(oi.quantity), 0) AS total_units_sold, COALESCE(AVG(r.rating), 0.0) AS avg_rating FROM [products] p LEFT JOIN [order_items] oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id LEFT JOIN [reviews] r ON p.product_id = r.product_id GROUP BY p.product_id, p.product_name ORDER BY total_units_sold DESC, avg_rating DESC;

clarification_points: Whether 'best performing' refers to sales volume (units sold), total revenue ($), or average customer review rating

test_cases.description: Ambiguous intent test where 'best performing' could mean revenue, units, or ratings.

test_cases.user_intent: Get the top 3 most expensive active products.
test_cases.gold_sql: SELECT product_name, unit_price FROM products WHERE is_active = 1 ORDER BY unit_price DESC LIMIT 3;

dialect_variations.sqlite: SELECT product_name, unit_price FROM products WHERE is_active = 1 ORDER BY unit_price DESC LIMIT 3;
dialect_variations.postgres: SELECT "product_name", "unit_price" FROM "products" WHERE "is_active" = 1 ORDER BY "unit_price" DESC LIMIT 3;
dialect_variations.tsql: SELECT TOP 3 [product_name], [unit_price] FROM [products] WHERE [is_active] = 1 ORDER BY [unit_price] DESC;

test_cases.description: Dialect differences (LIMIT vs TOP) with active status filter and ordering.
